{"schema_version":"teaching-unit.v0.4.0","input_manifest_sha256":"d0578d85a48ecc6924a83a8117e4c6d04c5641e9e72b2f367406a016592c81b7","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-nv-class-c:lineage:59","source_registry_sha256":"3e184808e042e052d0c78d0dff47c50b34a56560f428649c492afe10bc7ba712","units":[{"unit_id":"sec11-u01","module_id":"sec11-m01","objective_ids":["sec11-u01"],"title":{"text":"Required insurance","fact_ids":["sec11-F01","sec11-R01","sec11-F02"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Every registered vehicle in Nevada must carry liability insurance, and the law sets minimum amounts.","fact_ids":["sec11-F01","sec11-F03","sec11-F04"]},{"text":"Letting coverage lapse brings fines and can cost you your license for a time.","fact_ids":["sec11-F06","sec11-F07"]},{"text":"You must be able to show proof of insurance from the vehicle.","fact_ids":["sec11-F02"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"A driver's insurance lapses for two months, and the DMV suspends the registration of the two vehicles on that policy.","fact_ids":["sec11-F06","sec11-R03"]},"reasoning":{"text":"With no replacement coverage for that period, the driver pays a reinstatement fee plus fines from two hundred fifty dollars up to one thousand seven hundred fifty dollars for each vehicle on the policy.","fact_ids":["sec11-F06","sec11-R03"]},"result":{"text":"The fines and the fee apply to both vehicles, and an SR-twenty-two or a thirty-day license suspension may also follow.","fact_ids":["sec11-R03","sec11-F07"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking lapse fines are charged once per driver.","fact_ids":["sec11-R03"]},"correction":{"text":"Lapse fines and the reinstatement fee apply to each registered vehicle that the lapsed policy covered.","fact_ids":["sec11-R03","sec11-F06"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Twenty-five, fifty, twenty: the liability minimums.","fact_ids":["sec11-F03","sec11-F04"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"A police officer asks for proof of insurance at a stop. In what forms may you show it?","fact_ids":["sec11-F02"]},"answer":{"text":"The insurer's card from the vehicle, or the electronic version on a mobile device.","fact_ids":["sec11-F02"]},"rationale":{"text":"Keep the insurer's Evidence of Insurance Card in the vehicle, or have it ready in electronic form to show on a mobile device.","fact_ids":["sec11-F02"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec11-u01-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Insurance is mandatory","fact_ids":["sec11-F01","sec11-R01"]},"lines":[{"text":"Liability insurance for every vehicle.","fact_ids":["sec11-F01","sec11-R01"]},{"text":"Minimum amounts set by law.","fact_ids":["sec11-F01","sec11-R01"]},{"text":"Penalties for a lapse.","fact_ids":["sec11-F01","sec11-R01"]}],"narration":{"text":"This lesson opens the chapter on insurance and financial responsibility. All Nevada motorists must comply with mandatory insurance and financial responsibility laws, and every registered motor vehicle in the state must be covered by liability insurance. Nevada law sets minimum liability insurance amounts that apply whenever you drive or own a vehicle in the state. We will cover how to carry proof of insurance, the minimum coverage amounts, the NV LIVE program that flags lapses, and the fines and other penalties that follow when coverage ends without a replacement.","fact_ids":["sec11-F01","sec11-R01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":36,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec11-u01-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Proof and minimums","fact_ids":["sec11-F02","sec11-F03","sec11-F01"]},"lines":[{"text":"Card in the car or on your phone.","fact_ids":["sec11-F02","sec11-F03","sec11-F01"]},{"text":"Twenty-five thousand for one person.","fact_ids":["sec11-F02","sec11-F03","sec11-F01"]},{"text":"Fifty thousand for two or more.","fact_ids":["sec11-F02","sec11-F03","sec11-F01"]}],"narration":{"text":"Keep the insurer's Evidence of Insurance Card in the vehicle, or have it ready in electronic form to show on a mobile device. Nevada's minimum liability coverage is twenty-five thousand dollars for injury or death of one person in a crash and fifty thousand dollars for injury or death of two or more people in one crash. Those are minimums, which means the policy may carry more but never less. Every registered motor vehicle in Nevada must be covered by liability insurance at no less than these amounts, whether you drive it or simply own it.","fact_ids":["sec11-F02","sec11-F03","sec11-F01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec11-u01-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Property and NV LIVE","fact_ids":["sec11-F04","sec11-F05"]},"lines":[{"text":"Twenty thousand for property damage.","fact_ids":["sec11-F04","sec11-F05"]},{"text":"NV LIVE flags lapses.","fact_ids":["sec11-F04","sec11-F05"]},{"text":"Works with licensed insurers.","fact_ids":["sec11-F04","sec11-F05"]}],"narration":{"text":"Nevada's minimum liability coverage also includes twenty thousand dollars for damage to or destruction of other people's property in any one crash. NV LIVE, the Nevada Liability Insurance Validation Electronically program, works with licensed insurers to flag registrations whose insurance has ended or lapsed. Registrations whose insurance has ended or lapsed are flagged through that program. Keeping the policy active without any gap is the only way to avoid the lapse penalties. The property minimum sits beside the two injury minimums of twenty-five and fifty thousand dollars.","fact_ids":["sec11-F04","sec11-F05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":35,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec11-u01-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Lapse penalties","fact_ids":["sec11-F06","sec11-R03","sec11-F07"]},"lines":[{"text":"Reinstatement fee plus fines.","fact_ids":["sec11-F06","sec11-R03","sec11-F07"]},{"text":"Fines per vehicle on the policy.","fact_ids":["sec11-F06","sec11-R03","sec11-F07"]},{"text":"SR-twenty-two or thirty-day suspension.","fact_ids":["sec11-F06","sec11-R03","sec11-F07"]}],"narration":{"text":"If a registration is suspended for an insurance lapse with no replacement coverage for that period, you pay a reinstatement fee plus fines starting at two hundred fifty dollars and reaching up to one thousand seven hundred fifty dollars for each vehicle on that policy. Lapse fines and the reinstatement fee apply to each registered vehicle that the lapsed policy covered. Further penalties for an insurance lapse can include an SR-twenty-two requirement, a thirty-day driver license suspension, or both. So a lapse affects the registration, the wallet and possibly the driver's license too.","fact_ids":["sec11-F06","sec11-R03","sec11-F07"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec11-u01-s5","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Per vehicle, not per driver","fact_ids":["sec11-R03","sec11-F06","sec11-F07"]},"lines":[{"text":"Fines apply to each vehicle.","fact_ids":["sec11-R03","sec11-F06","sec11-F07"]},{"text":"A family policy multiplies the cost.","fact_ids":["sec11-R03","sec11-F06","sec11-F07"]},{"text":"Other penalties may follow.","fact_ids":["sec11-R03","sec11-F06","sec11-F07"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap. Some drivers assume a lapse brings one fine, charged to the driver. The handbook says lapse fines and the reinstatement fee apply to each registered vehicle that the lapsed policy covered. A policy that covered three vehicles means fines and fees for all three. On top of that, the lapse can bring an SR-twenty-two requirement, a thirty-day license suspension, or both. So when a question asks about the cost of a lapse, count the vehicles on the policy, and remember that the license itself may also be at risk.","fact_ids":["sec11-R03","sec11-F06","sec11-F07"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec11-u01-s6","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check proof of insurance","fact_ids":["sec11-F02","sec11-F03","sec11-F04"]},"lines":[{"text":"An officer asks for proof.","fact_ids":["sec11-F02","sec11-F03","sec11-F04"]},{"text":"What forms are accepted?","fact_ids":["sec11-F02","sec11-F03","sec11-F04"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: at a traffic stop, an officer asks for proof of insurance. In what forms may you show it? Recall the rule before reading on. You may show the Evidence of Insurance Card from your insurer, kept in the vehicle, or the same proof in electronic form on a mobile device. Either works. Behind that proof must be real coverage that meets Nevada's minimums: twenty-five thousand dollars for one person, fifty thousand dollars for two or more people, and twenty thousand dollars for property damage in one crash.","fact_ids":["sec11-F02","sec11-F03","sec11-F04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec11-u01-s7","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Insurance recap","fact_ids":["sec11-F01","sec11-R01","sec11-F02","sec11-F03","sec11-F04","sec11-F05","sec11-F06","sec11-R03","sec11-F07"]},"lines":[{"text":"Liability insurance is mandatory.","fact_ids":["sec11-F01","sec11-R01","sec11-F02","sec11-F03","sec11-F04","sec11-F05","sec11-F06","sec11-R03","sec11-F07"]},{"text":"Know the three minimums.","fact_ids":["sec11-F01","sec11-R01","sec11-F02","sec11-F03","sec11-F04","sec11-F05","sec11-F06","sec11-R03","sec11-F07"]},{"text":"Lapses cost per vehicle.","fact_ids":["sec11-F01","sec11-R01","sec11-F02","sec11-F03","sec11-F04","sec11-F05","sec11-F06","sec11-R03","sec11-F07"]}],"narration":{"text":"To review, every registered vehicle in Nevada must carry liability insurance, and the minimums apply whenever you drive or own a vehicle. Carry the insurance card in the vehicle or on your phone. The minimums are twenty-five thousand dollars for one person, fifty thousand dollars for two or more people, and twenty thousand dollars for property damage in one crash. NV LIVE flags lapses. A lapse with no replacement coverage brings a reinstatement fee and fines from two hundred fifty to one thousand seven hundred fifty dollars per vehicle, and possibly an SR-twenty-two or a thirty-day suspension.","fact_ids":["sec11-F01","sec11-R01","sec11-F02","sec11-F03","sec11-F04","sec11-F05","sec11-F06","sec11-R03","sec11-F07"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec11-u02","module_id":"sec11-m02","objective_ids":["sec11-u02"],"title":{"text":"Reporting crashes","fact_ids":["sec11-F08","sec11-F09","sec11-R02"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Every crash with injuries or significant damage must reach the DMV, either through the police or through your own report.","fact_ids":["sec11-F08","sec11-F09","sec11-R02"]},{"text":"The DMV decides fault and liability, and uninsured or unreported crashes bring suspensions.","fact_ids":["sec11-F11","sec11-F12","sec11-F13"]},{"text":"The SR-twenty-two is how the DMV monitors insurance for drivers being reinstated.","fact_ids":["sec11-F14","sec11-F15"]},{"text":"The SR-twenty-two is filed once and bought only when everything else for reinstatement is done.","fact_ids":["sec11-F15"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Two drivers have a crash in a parking lot that police do not investigate, with about one thousand dollars in damage.","fact_ids":["sec11-F09","sec11-R02"]},"reasoning":{"text":"If police do not investigate a crash that causes seven hundred fifty dollars or more in damage or injures anyone, you must send the SR-one to the DMV within ten days.","fact_ids":["sec11-F09","sec11-R02"]},"result":{"text":"Both drivers must send an SR-one within ten days, since anyone who was a driver or registered owner must complete it.","fact_ids":["sec11-F09","sec11-F10"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking the SR-one and the SR-twenty-two are the same form.","fact_ids":["sec11-R04"]},"correction":{"text":"The SR-one is a crash report you file, while the SR-twenty-two is proof-of-insurance coverage the DMV monitors when reinstating a suspended or revoked driver.","fact_ids":["sec11-R04","sec11-F14"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"SR-one reports the crash; SR-twenty-two proves the coverage.","fact_ids":["sec11-R04"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"When does SR-twenty-two coverage start, and how often do you file the form?","fact_ids":["sec11-F15"]},"answer":{"text":"It starts when you actually reinstate, and you file it only once.","fact_ids":["sec11-F15"]},"rationale":{"text":"SR-twenty-two coverage starts when you actually reinstate, you file the form only once, and you should not buy it until every other reinstatement requirement is met.","fact_ids":["sec11-F15"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec11-u02-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"After a crash: the paperwork","fact_ids":["sec11-F08","sec11-F09","sec11-F14"]},"lines":[{"text":"How crashes reach the DMV.","fact_ids":["sec11-F08","sec11-F09","sec11-F14"]},{"text":"The SR-one crash report.","fact_ids":["sec11-F08","sec11-F09","sec11-F14"]},{"text":"The SR-twenty-two.","fact_ids":["sec11-F08","sec11-F09","sec11-F14"]}],"narration":{"text":"This lesson covers the paperwork side of a crash. When law enforcement investigates a crash, the officer sends your insurance information and a description of the damage or injuries to the DMV. When police do not investigate, the duty to report may fall on you. We will cover when you must file an SR-one and who files it, how the DMV decides fault and liability, what happens to drivers without insurance or who fail to report, and what an SR-twenty-two is, when it starts, and when to buy it. Getting this right keeps your license and registration safe.","fact_ids":["sec11-F08","sec11-F09","sec11-F14"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec11-u02-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"The SR-one","fact_ids":["sec11-F09","sec11-F10"]},"lines":[{"text":"No police report: you may need to file.","fact_ids":["sec11-F09","sec11-F10"]},{"text":"Seven hundred fifty dollars or any injury.","fact_ids":["sec11-F09","sec11-F10"]},{"text":"File within ten days.","fact_ids":["sec11-F09","sec11-F10"]}],"narration":{"text":"If police do not investigate a crash that causes seven hundred fifty dollars or more in damage or injures anyone, you must send a Report of Crash Form, the SR-one, to the DMV within ten days. The SR-one must be completed by anyone who was the driver or the registered owner of a vehicle in the crash, and the form is available at DMV offices, the Nevada Highway Patrol, local police and the DMV website. So in an uninvestigated crash, more than one person may need to file: every driver and every registered owner involved.","fact_ids":["sec11-F09","sec11-F10"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec11-u02-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Fault and consequences","fact_ids":["sec11-F11","sec11-F12","sec11-F13"]},"lines":[{"text":"The DMV decides fault and liability.","fact_ids":["sec11-F11","sec11-F12","sec11-F13"]},{"text":"Uninsured at fault: suspension or deposit.","fact_ids":["sec11-F11","sec11-F12","sec11-F13"]},{"text":"Unreported crash: suspension.","fact_ids":["sec11-F11","sec11-F12","sec11-F13"]}],"narration":{"text":"After a crash, the DMV Financial Responsibility Section decides who was at fault, whether every vehicle and driver was insured, and the total liability. An at-fault driver without liability insurance may have the license or registration suspended, must post a deposit with the DMV to cover crash costs, or must arrange payment with the other parties. Failing to report a crash to the DMV can lead to suspension of your driver license, your vehicle registration, or both. So both missing insurance and a missing report carry the same kind of risk: losing the right to drive or register.","fact_ids":["sec11-F11","sec11-F12","sec11-F13"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec11-u02-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"The SR-twenty-two","fact_ids":["sec11-F14","sec11-F15","sec11-R05"]},"lines":[{"text":"Monitored liability insurance on a license.","fact_ids":["sec11-F14","sec11-F15","sec11-R05"]},{"text":"Starts when you reinstate.","fact_ids":["sec11-F14","sec11-F15","sec11-R05"]},{"text":"File once; buy it last.","fact_ids":["sec11-F14","sec11-F15","sec11-R05"]}],"narration":{"text":"An SR-twenty-two is liability insurance on a driver license that lets the DMV monitor the insurance of a suspended or revoked driver through reports from the insurer, and it may be required for reinstatement. SR-twenty-two coverage starts when you actually reinstate, you file the form only once, and you should not buy it until every other reinstatement requirement is met. The price of SR-twenty-two coverage depends on how the insurance company structures it. So the SR-twenty-two is the final step of reinstatement, not the first, and its cost varies by insurer.","fact_ids":["sec11-F14","sec11-F15","sec11-R05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":36,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec11-u02-s5","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Two report paths","fact_ids":["sec11-R02","sec11-F08","sec11-F09"]},"lines":[{"text":"Police investigate: officer reports.","fact_ids":["sec11-R02","sec11-F08","sec11-F09"]},{"text":"No police: you file the SR-one.","fact_ids":["sec11-R02","sec11-F08","sec11-F09"]},{"text":"Threshold: injury or seven hundred fifty dollars.","fact_ids":["sec11-R02","sec11-F08","sec11-F09"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap. Some drivers think a crash reaches the DMV automatically every time; others think it never needs a report unless police are called. The handbook sets two paths. A police-investigated crash reaches the DMV through the officer's report. A crash without police investigation that injures anyone or causes seven hundred fifty dollars or more in damage needs your own SR-one within ten days. So the first question is whether police investigated. If not, check the injuries and the damage amount, and file the SR-one if either threshold is met.","fact_ids":["sec11-R02","sec11-F08","sec11-F09"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec11-u02-s6","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"SR-one or SR-twenty-two?","fact_ids":["sec11-R04","sec11-F09","sec11-F14"]},"lines":[{"text":"SR-one: a crash report you file.","fact_ids":["sec11-R04","sec11-F09","sec11-F14"]},{"text":"SR-twenty-two: monitored insurance proof.","fact_ids":["sec11-R04","sec11-F09","sec11-F14"]},{"text":"Different forms, different purposes.","fact_ids":["sec11-R04","sec11-F09","sec11-F14"]}],"narration":{"text":"The SR-one is a crash report you file, while the SR-twenty-two is proof-of-insurance coverage that the DMV monitors when reinstating a suspended or revoked driver. They share a prefix, which makes them easy to mix up. Think of the SR-one as the form you send within ten days of an uninvestigated crash with injuries or enough damage, and the SR-twenty-two as the coverage an insurer reports on for a driver coming back from a suspension or revocation. One describes an event; the other proves ongoing insurance for reinstatement.","fact_ids":["sec11-R04","sec11-F09","sec11-F14"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":35,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec11-u02-s7","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check the SR-twenty-two","fact_ids":["sec11-F15","sec11-F14","sec11-R05"]},"lines":[{"text":"Reinstating a suspended license.","fact_ids":["sec11-F15","sec11-F14","sec11-R05"]},{"text":"When does the coverage start?","fact_ids":["sec11-F15","sec11-F14","sec11-R05"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: a driver is getting a suspended license reinstated and needs an SR-twenty-two. When does the coverage start, and how often is the form filed? Recall the rule before reading on. The coverage starts when the driver actually reinstates, and the form is filed only once. The handbook adds that you should not buy SR-twenty-two coverage until every other reinstatement requirement is met, and that its price depends on how the insurance company structures it. It lets the DMV monitor the driver's insurance through reports from the insurer.","fact_ids":["sec11-F15","sec11-F14","sec11-R05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec11-u02-s8","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Reporting recap","fact_ids":["sec11-F08","sec11-F09","sec11-F10","sec11-F11","sec11-F12","sec11-F13","sec11-F14","sec11-F15","sec11-R02","sec11-R04"]},"lines":[{"text":"Officer reports investigated crashes.","fact_ids":["sec11-F08","sec11-F09","sec11-F10","sec11-F11","sec11-F12","sec11-F13","sec11-F14","sec11-F15","sec11-R02","sec11-R04"]},{"text":"SR-one within ten days otherwise.","fact_ids":["sec11-F08","sec11-F09","sec11-F10","sec11-F11","sec11-F12","sec11-F13","sec11-F14","sec11-F15","sec11-R02","sec11-R04"]},{"text":"SR-twenty-two for reinstatement.","fact_ids":["sec11-F08","sec11-F09","sec11-F10","sec11-F11","sec11-F12","sec11-F13","sec11-F14","sec11-F15","sec11-R02","sec11-R04"]}],"narration":{"text":"To sum up, when police investigate a crash, the officer sends the insurance details and damage description to the DMV. When they do not, a crash with injuries or seven hundred fifty dollars or more in damage needs an SR-one within ten days from every driver and registered owner. The DMV decides fault, insurance and liability. An uninsured at-fault driver faces suspension, a deposit or arranged payment, and failing to report can suspend the license or registration. An SR-twenty-two is monitored insurance for reinstatement, filed once and bought last.","fact_ids":["sec11-F08","sec11-F09","sec11-F10","sec11-F11","sec11-F12","sec11-F13","sec11-F14","sec11-F15","sec11-R02","sec11-R04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":36,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec11-u03","module_id":"sec11-m03","objective_ids":["sec11-u03"],"title":{"text":"At the crash scene","fact_ids":["sec11-F16","sec11-F17","sec11-R06"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Knowing what to do in the first minutes after a crash protects the injured, warns other drivers and meets the law.","fact_ids":["sec11-F16","sec11-F18"]},{"text":"Even a minor crash with an empty parked car has a duty attached.","fact_ids":["sec11-F19"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"A driver has a minor fender bender on a busy street; no one is hurt and both cars can be driven.","fact_ids":["sec11-F17"]},"reasoning":{"text":"With only property damage and no injuries, move the vehicle if it can be moved safely to a spot that does not block traffic, then return to the scene.","fact_ids":["sec11-F17","sec11-R06"]},"result":{"text":"Both drivers move to a safe spot nearby, return, and exchange their information.","fact_ids":["sec11-F17","sec11-F18"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking you may drive off after hitting a parked car if no one is around.","fact_ids":["sec11-F19"]},"correction":{"text":"If you hit an unattended vehicle or other property, give the owner your name, address, license number, registration and insurance details, in person or in a note left behind.","fact_ids":["sec11-F19"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Stop, help, warn, notify, then exchange.","fact_ids":["sec11-F16","sec11-F18"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"What information must you give other drivers after a crash?","fact_ids":["sec11-F18"]},"answer":{"text":"Your name, address, driver license number, registration and insurance information.","fact_ids":["sec11-F18"]},"rationale":{"text":"Exchange your name, address, driver license number, registration and insurance information with every other driver involved.","fact_ids":["sec11-F18"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec11-u03-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Your duties at a crash","fact_ids":["sec11-F16","sec11-F17"]},"lines":[{"text":"First steps.","fact_ids":["sec11-F16","sec11-F17"]},{"text":"Fender benders.","fact_ids":["sec11-F16","sec11-F17"]},{"text":"Exchanging information.","fact_ids":["sec11-F16","sec11-F17"]}],"narration":{"text":"This lesson covers what to do at the scene of a crash. The first duties are the same in every crash: stop, get medical help for anyone injured, warn traffic and notify law enforcement. After that, the handbook covers moving a minor fender bender out of the way, exchanging information with the other drivers, and what to do when you hit a vehicle or property with no one around. These steps protect the people involved and other road users, and they also make sure the crash is handled lawfully afterward. Each step has its place in the order.","fact_ids":["sec11-F16","sec11-F17"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec11-u03-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"The first duties","fact_ids":["sec11-F16","sec11-R06"]},"lines":[{"text":"Stop.","fact_ids":["sec11-F16","sec11-R06"]},{"text":"Get medical help; warn traffic.","fact_ids":["sec11-F16","sec11-R06"]},{"text":"Notify law enforcement.","fact_ids":["sec11-F16","sec11-R06"]}],"narration":{"text":"At a crash, stop, get medical help for anyone injured, warn traffic and notify law enforcement. If a crash involves injuries, the first duties are to stop, get medical help and warn traffic; the move-it-aside rule covers a fender bender with property damage only and a vehicle that can be moved safely. So injuries change the order: helping people and protecting the scene come before anything else. Only when no one is hurt and the cars can be driven does the handbook direct you to clear the roadway first and return to the scene afterward.","fact_ids":["sec11-F16","sec11-R06"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec11-u03-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Fender benders and information","fact_ids":["sec11-F17","sec11-F18"]},"lines":[{"text":"No injuries: move aside, then return.","fact_ids":["sec11-F17","sec11-F18"]},{"text":"Exchange five pieces of information.","fact_ids":["sec11-F17","sec11-F18"]},{"text":"With every other driver.","fact_ids":["sec11-F17","sec11-F18"]}],"narration":{"text":"In a fender bender with only property damage and no injuries, move the vehicle if it can be moved safely to a spot that does not block traffic, then return to the scene. Exchange your name, address, driver license number, registration and insurance information with every other driver involved. Those five details are the same ones you would leave in a note for the owner of an unattended vehicle.
